newsitem.title: CHINA: China says ties with U.S. should have no obstacles.
newsitem.headline: China says ties with U.S. should have no obstacles.

text.p: China on Tuesday praised the recent warming of Sino-U.S. ties and said differences between Washington and Beijing should not be obstacles to improving relations between the two Pacific giants.
China's relations with the United States had improved steadily in recent months despite differences of opinion in some areas, Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a regular news briefing.
"These differences should not be made into obstacles that affect the strengthening of international cooperation between our two nations," he said.
Relations between Beijing and Washington would continue to improve as long as differences did not turn into obstacles, Shen said.
Shen was responding to a question about China's views on recent comments on Sino-U.S. relations by newly appointed U.S. Secretary of State Madeline Albright.

Albright has vowed to confront Beijing on its human rights record, trade issues and weapon sales abroad -- all thorns in Sino-U.S. ties -- but says relations between the two Pacific giants cannot be held hostage to any one issue.
Beijing and Washington have long been at loggerheads over such issues as human rights, Taiwan and trade.
Shen said there were many areas for further cooperation between China and the United States and the two faced many opportunities as well as challenges.
"The crucial thing... is how to grasp the opportunities," Shen said.
Upcoming exchanges of high-level officials between the two sides would further boost recovering ties, Shen said. U.S. Vice President Al Gore may visit China as early as March.
